searchText: That's tricky. The spec doesn't say anything about this ancestor of the head of the canonical chain, it could be more specific by saying that *if an ancestor is `VALID`* (assuming full validation) the update may be skipped. This would be enough to rely on the invariant that CL never sends an fcU if a beacon block enveloping the head is invalid. Thus CL will either extend the canonical chain or switch a fork by the subsequent fcU calls. I agree with that, I wish the spec were stricter in this particular case. The reason behind the MAY is because we didn't want to enforce any specific EL's behaviour as from the protocol's standpoint either way would be correct <@892053833121923094> do we have a test scenario reflecting this case? rpc.dencun seems to have gone down devnet-9 has been stopped: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1167472287050637453 It has the old kzg setup and client branches have moved on so we decided to stop it. devnet-11 will be launched soon and will stick around for a bit if there are no big changes. Not yet, but let me think about it because I think it should be possible but not straight-forward to do so in hive I am hesitant to make the forkchoice state update semantics depending on the `payloadAttributes` unless we see a strong reason for that

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
That's tricky. The spec doesn't say anything about this ancestor of the head of the canonical chain, it could be more specific by saying that *if an ancestor is `VALID`* (assuming full validation) the update may be skipped.

This would be enough to rely on the invariant that CL never sends an fcU if a beacon block enveloping the head is invalid. Thus CL will either extend the canonical chain or switch a fork by the subsequent fcU calls.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: I agree with that, I wish the spec were stricter in this particular case. The reason behind the MAY is because we didn't want to enforce any specific EL's behaviour as from the protocol's standpoint either way would be correct
